# Closure follow-up — 2026-09-14

Scope: bounded adversarial follow-up to [workflow delivery](2026-09-13-governed-workflows.md),
not a new feature program. Existing consumer pins, native coverage and release limits
remain unchanged. User-owned intent-distribution and consumer UI changes are preserved.

## Repaired: wire-level identity normalization

The Go-input guard from INC-12 cannot detect a malformed escape after `encoding/json`
has replaced it. A model fact reference `\ud800` or `\udfff` became U+FFFD and matched
an actual fact with that ID; a passing reviewed artifact resulted. The CLI similarly
accepted altered principals, and lesson bundles accepted changed descriptive identities.

`internal/jsonwire.ValidUnicode` now guards the existing strict decoders before that
lossy conversion. It checks raw UTF-8 and escaped surrogate pairing without allocation,
state or dependencies. Existing syntax, duplicate-key, shape and resource checks remain
in their owners. Valid pairs, literal U+FFFD and escaped backslashes still work.
No existing consumer API signature changed; this is INC-13, not a source-truth claim.

Evidence:

- Focused uncached race suites: private guard, sourced prose, lesson transfer,
  sourced-prose scenario and workflow CLI passed.
- Every standalone UTF-16 code unit is tested (65,536 cases). A bounded two-worker
  fuzz run completed 84,493 executions without failure; this is implementation evidence,
  not statistical production reliability.
- A temporary Go overlay disabled only escaped-scalar validation, retaining raw UTF-8
  checks. The model, CLI check/export and all three lesson-file regressions then failed;
  correctly rebound lesson hashes ensure this tests decoding, not incidental digest drift.
- Independent focused review reported no issue. Root `task validate` passed;
  Fathom separately verified all 13 workflow implementation rows.
- resume_as_code's `cmd/llm` and `cmd/redteam` passed uncached race tests against the
  proposed kit through a temporary readonly modfile and pinned app-kit snapshot.
  `go list` confirmed the actual proposed lesson/helper directories; no consumer file
  or pin was changed. The other three inspected consumer build/test graphs import
  neither affected kit. This is compatibility evidence, not another production adoption.

## Remaining plan work and Fathom value

The eight open rows in [Fathom uplift asks](../plans/fathom-uplift-asks.md) are distinct
from the 13 completed workflow implementation rows. FA-13/14/18 need cross-repository
agreement; FA-15/19 depend on proposed annotation/routing decisions; FA-22 is explicitly
deferred; FA-17 changes prohibited global configuration. FA-16 can integrate structured
Fathom audits but overlaps the owner's in-progress distributed skill changes; no edits
were made to those files and no backlog row was relabelled complete.

The installed `fathom intent audit -json` completed successfully in 1.30 seconds and
reported all 48 read outcomes available. Useful: machine-readable scope and unproven
claims, with evidence paths. Limits: task-based gates are not necessarily `Test*` hooks;
historical unannotated plans are not current workflow failures; a missing generated
guard artifact is not proof that the repository's actual hook is absent. Those findings
require interpretation, not automatic repair. The audit also reported the router's
illustrative `*/schema.cue` label unmatched by its glob parser; prose scope labels
are not executable proof.
Two `fathom plans` scans failed to return within the review's wait window; checklist
enumeration supplied the eight-row answer. Their processes exited; none were left running.

Net: Fathom remains useful for navigation and structured audit inputs, but its parser
scope and failure/timeout behavior must stay visible. Small delegated tasks, scoped
rechecks and one short fuzz run added evidence without more paid model verification.
